hook_text: The letters on your phone's keyboard are in the same strange order as on typewriters from 150 years ago.
clip_script: A dusty storeroom in a school in Kimberley. Under a cloth sits a heavy black machine with round keys. The school secretary rolls in a sheet of paper and starts to type. Clack, clack, clack: metal arms jump up and hit an inky ribbon, and letters appear on the page. Ding! A bell rings at the end of the line, and she pushes a lever to start the next one. No plug, no screen, no electricity. Just fingers and clever machinery.
visual_style: Whiteboard drawing of a manual typewriter with labelled keys, typebars, ribbon, carriage and bell, then a phone keyboard showing the same QWERTY letters.
mood: Playful and noisy, like a machine making music.
pacing: Rhythmic clacks building up, a ding at each turn, then a quick jump to today's keyboards.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and look at the first six letters on any keyboard.
